I have resolved the issue where email messages crashed on non-ASCII domain names when the email encoding was non-Unicode:

- Added [`punycode()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mz83e_iy/django/utils/encoding.py#L221-L223) in [encoding.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mz83e_iy/django/utils/encoding.py) to convert non-ASCII domains to Punycode (`domain.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`).
- Updated [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mz83e_iy/django/core/mail/utils.py#L16-L19) in [utils.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mz83e_iy/django/core/mail/utils.py) and [`EmailMessage.message()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mz83e_iy/django/core/mail/message.py#L255-L257) / [`sanitize_address()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mz83e_iy/django/core/mail/message.py#L74-L108) in [message.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mz83e_iy/django/core/mail/message.py) (as well as [validators.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mz83e_iy/django/core/validators.py) and [html.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mz83e_iy/django/utils/html.py)) to convert domain names to Punycode.
